newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols near flat in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols near flat in quiet trade.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were little changed Thursday as the underlying futures finished the day on a strong note.

July options volatility ended a touch higher at 8.30 percent, up from 8.25 percent on the opening and Wednesday's close. September was 8.50 percent, down from 8.55 percent on the opening but up slightly from the previous day's settlement.

Floor traders said the day's highlight in options was a bet that volatility would rebound from the current weak levels. The firm executing the trade bought 1,000 July 109-00 straddles covered in futures when the June bond contract was at 108-20.
The volatility buyer could be looking for upcoming economic indicators to provide a catalyst for a price breakout, traders said.
"You've still got plenty of time left in July for them to make a move," a dealer for a U.S. banking firm said of the July options.
Otherwise, trading in options was described as light.
June futures ended 19/32 higher at 109-10, still caught in a comfortable range.

Revisions to first-quarter U.S. gross domestic product data will be released Friday morning, with growth forecast at a revised 6.0 percent, from the government's previous estimate of 5.6 percent. U.S. April new home sales, also due out Friday, are forecast down slightly.

Volatilities for Eurodollar options were unchanged at 9.0 percent in September and 10.9 percent in December. Trading interest focused on short-dated June 93.50 straddles and put spread combinations in front-month quarterly options, floor dealers said.
